title: Inert-active factorization and orthogonality in a symmetric infinity operad
statement:
Use quasicategories, mapping spaces and coherent triangles of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and symmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Let $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be a small symmetric infinity operad. A pointed map is active when the inverse image of its basepoint consists only of the basepoint; call an edge of $P$ active when its image is active. Inert edges of $P$ are the $p$-cocartesian edges over inert pointed maps, as in the cited definition.

Every edge $b:x\to y$ admits a coherent factorization $x\xrightarrow{i}z\xrightarrow{a}y$, with $i$ inert and $a$ active. Moreover, for every inert edge $i:x\to y$ and active edge $a:u\to v$, the composition-induced comparison of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_P(y,u)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_P(x,u)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_P(x,v)}\operatorname{Map}_P(y,v)$$
is an equivalence. Here the maps to $\operatorname{Map}_P(x,v)$ are postcomposition with $a$ and precomposition with $i$. The homotopy pullback retains the specified homotopy making a square commute. Thus the space of diagonal fillers of each coherent square with left side $i$ and right side $a$, including its two compatible triangles and all higher compatibility data, is contractible. The assertion includes arity zero.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 2.1.2.3 and Proposition 2.1.2.4, deduced from Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5; printed pp. 178-179 Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $B=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and write $H(S,T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Fin}_*}(S,T)$, regarded as a discrete space. From the nerve and right-pinched mapping-space definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $\operatorname{Map}_B(S,T)=H(S,T)$: a simplex has all its initial arrows equal to identities, so every remaining arrow is the same pointed map. Also $B$ is a quasicategory, since an inner horn in an ordinary nerve extends by composition of its string of arrows. By [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], $p$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts of inert maps. Hence $P$ is a quasicategory: extend the image of an inner horn in $B$, then lift that extension using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. This checks the hypotheses of the cocartesian mapping-space criterion used below.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10 and Definition 2.1.2.3; explicit nerve and inner-horn checks

proof.text: For $b:x\to y$, let $\alpha=p(b):\langle m\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$. Set $S=\{t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\alpha(t)\ne *\}$, choose a bijection $e:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to S$ with $k=|S|$, and define $r:\langle m\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$ by $r(e(j))=j$ and $r(t)=*$ off $S$. Define $s:\langle k\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ by $s(j)=\alpha(e(j))$ for $j\ne *$. Then $r$ is inert, $s$ is active, and $sr=\alpha$. This is a direct check of the inert condition in [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition] and the active condition $s^{-1}(*)=\{*\}$; it also applies when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.2; explicit factorization by the non-discarded inputs

proof.text: Choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $i:x\to z$ of $r$ using [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Apply the outer-horn condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] in dimension two: the horn $\Lambda^2_0$ has edge $01=i$ and edge $02=b$, and its prescribed base $2$-simplex has edges $r,s,\alpha$. Its filler supplies an edge $a:z\to y$ over $s$ and a $2$-simplex with boundary $i,a,b$. Thus $i$ is inert, $a$ is active, and this is a coherent factorization of the given edge, rather than only an equality of homotopy classes.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5, proof (3), specialized to the factorization of Remark 2.1.2.2; dimension-two cocartesian lifting

proof.text: We next check orthogonality in the base explicitly. Let $r:X\to Y$ be inert, $s:U\to V$ active, and let $f:X\to U$, $g:Y\to V$ satisfy $sf=gr$. For $t\in r^{-1}(*)$, this equality gives $s(f(t))=*$, hence $f(t)=*$ by activity. For each $j\in Y\setminus\{*\}$ let $t_j$ be its unique preimage under $r$, and set $d(j)=f(t_j)$ and $d(*)=*$. Then $dr=f$ (including on discarded elements) and $sd=g$ (evaluate at each $t_j$ and at $*$). These formulas force every value of $d$, so the filler is unique. Consequently the square with rows $H(Y,U)\to H(X,U)$ and $H(Y,V)\to H(X,V)$, with vertical maps given by postcomposition with $s$, is a pullback of discrete spaces, and hence a homotopy pullback. The construction does not require $Y$ or $U$ to have a non-basepoint.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, proof (2); direct pointed-set filler calculation

proof.text:
Fix the inert $i:x\to y$ and active $a:u\to v$ of the statement. Write $X=p(x)$, $Y=p(y)$, $U=p(u)$, $V=p(v)$, and $M(t,w)=\operatorname{Map}_P(t,w)$. Consider the three-row diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}M(y,u)&\longrightarrow&M(x,u)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ H(Y,U)&\longrightarrow&H(X,U)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ H(Y,V)&\longrightarrow&H(X,V).\end{array}$$
The first square is a homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for the $p$-cocartesian edge $i$ with test vertex $u$; the second is a homotopy pullback by step 4 with $r=p(i)$ and $s=p(a)$. Pasting by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] shows that the outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback. Now compare with the three-row diagram whose rows are $M(y,u)\to M(x,u)$, $M(y,v)\to M(x,v)$ and $H(Y,V)\to H(X,V)$. Its lower square is a homotopy pullback by the same cocartesian criterion with test vertex $v$. Its outer rectangle is the one just proved to be a homotopy pullback, so cancellation in the pasting lemma makes its upper square a homotopy pullback. Here the vertical mapping-space maps are postcomposition with $a$, and the horizontal ones are precomposition with $i$. The commutation homotopies and their images under $p$ are the composition homotopies supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]; the outer homotopy is their concatenation, as required by the pasting statement. Pasting is applied to the transposed diagrams, merely interchanging the two coordinates in the path-space definition of a homotopy pullback. Therefore the resulting comparison is exactly
$$M(y,u)\longrightarrow M(x,u)\times^h_{M(x,v)}M(y,v),$$
with the specified square homotopy retained.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5, proof (2); mapping-space proof of the lift from base orthogonality, expanded using the existing cocartesian criterion and homotopy-pullback pasting

proof.text: Let $T=M(x,u)\times^h_{M(x,v)}M(y,v)$ and let $c:M(y,u)\to T$ be the comparison of step 5. A specified coherent square is a point $(f,g,h)$ of $T$. In the homotopy-fiber convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], its space of diagonal fillers is $\operatorname{hofib}_{(f,g,h)}(c)$: a point specifies a diagonal and a path from its induced square to $(f,g,h)$, so it contains both triangle homotopies and their compatibility with $h$, together with all higher simplices. Since $c$ is an equivalence, apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with $X=M(y,u)$, $Y=S=T$, $r=u=c$, $q=v=\mathrm{id}_T$ and the identity commutation homotopy. It identifies each homotopy fiber of $c$ with that of $\mathrm{id}_T$. The latter is contractible: its path-space model consists of paths ending at the specified point, and the simplicial map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ induced by $\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ contracts it: send a path $\gamma$ at parameter $s$ to the path $t\mapsto\gamma(\max(t,s))$. At $s=0$ this is $\gamma$, at $s=1$ it is constant at the specified endpoint, and the endpoint remains fixed throughout. This proves the asserted contractibility while retaining the square's specified homotopy. If $T$ is empty there are no squares to check.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5, proof (2); homotopy-fiber interpretation of the space of compatible fillers

proof.text: All constructions include arity zero. If $\alpha$ discards every input then $k=0$ in step 2, the lift in step 3 is an inert edge to the zero fiber, and the following map $\langle0\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ is active. If $n=0$, then $S$ is empty and the active factor is the identity of $\langle0\rangle$. In step 4, when $Y=\langle0\rangle$, activity forces $f$ to be the constant pointed map and the unique $d$ has source $\langle0\rangle$. When $U=\langle0\rangle$, both $f$ and $d$ are uniquely determined and the commutative-square condition forces $g$ to be constant since $r$ is surjective. Steps 5 and 6 impose no nonemptiness on mapping spaces. Thus neither the factorization nor orthogonality excluded any nullary case.

source.place: Definitions 2.1.1.10 and 2.1.2.3 and Proposition 2.1.2.4; explicit zero-arity verification

proof_origin.place: Remark 2.1.2.2, Definition 2.1.2.3, Proposition 2.1.2.4 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, proof (2)-(3), printed pp. 178-179. Read online; WANTED archived source. The general transport argument is expanded directly using existing mapping-space and pasting nodes, with explicit pointed-set calculations.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and ancestry. Gave explicit finite-pointed-set factorization and unique fillers; lifted the factorization by the defining cocartesian outer horn, and proved the full mapping-space comparison by two applications of existing homotopy-pullback pasting. Explained its contractible homotopy fibers and every zero-arity case. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. Initial absence of the item resolved when the shared snapshot refreshed.
split_report.blueprint: Supports the inherited exact place in prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, proof paragraph 2 (derived coefficient adjunction and finite-level mapping comparison), through the operadic approximation/monadic-bar ancestry recorded in blueprint.from: steps 1-3 construct the inert-active factorization, steps 4-6 prove orthogonality including coherent fillers, and step 7 checks arity zero. This is a supporting combinatorial input, not a replacement of the coefficient route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-4386549e9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all seven steps in full, along with the statements of the seven cited nodes and HA §2.1.2 (Def 2.1.2.1/2.1.2.3, Rem 2.1.2.2, Prop 2.1.2.4, and Prop 2.1.2.5 with proof (1)-(3), pp. 178-179) from the fetched PDF. The statement is HA 2.1.2.4 without the retract-closure clause, so it is true and not stronger than the source. Step 1: P is a quasicategory because B is one and p is an inner fibration, and the right-pinched Map in N(Fin_*) is discrete. Steps 2-3: the base inert/active factorization, then a Λ^2_0 cocartesian filler for n=2; this is HA 2.1.2.5(3). Step 4: base orthogonality in Fin_*, using activity, surjectivity of inert maps and uniqueness, with the ⟨0⟩ cases rechecked. Step 5: the cocartesian mapping criterion with test vertices u and v, plus pasting and cancellation. Both outer rectangles agree because their bottom row is discrete, and transposition is harmless because the cited homotopy-pullback notion fixes no orientation; this is HA 2.1.2.5(2). Step 6: fiber detection with q=v=id_T, and the path fibre of id_T is contracted by max. Step 7: arity zero. The cited nodes say what each step uses. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and there is no cycle (456 nodes traversed). All statement citations are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed, and no SGA source is used. The delivery creates no new nodes and I made no fixes. For the maintainer, not a fault of this delivery: the existing unsplit node lem-coef-operadic-inert-active-factorization (NU, 2026-10-17) overlaps this item and should be merged or made to cite it.
